chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it records the senior-track near-win: a Secret Super Battle player who did not take first, but still placed high enough for the event machine to print their name, region, rank, and route into a trophy card.

key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori

key_artists.why: Sugimori matters because the runner-up credential still uses the franchise's central early visual language. The card's rank is second, but its visual authority is not secondary.

claims.text: The local catalog models the World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional second-place source group as one row containing No.2 Trainer at source index 178.
Bulbapedia says No.2 Trainer began as a Japanese tournament Trainer card and later became a second-place prize in the Pokémon World Championships.

Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.2 Trainer iteration was first awarded to the runners-up of each regional Japanese World Challenge Summer event held between July and August 2000, with the circuit split into Tropical Mega Battle and Secret Super Battle events and retaining the age-limited structure.

Bulbapedia says top-ranking players from Secret Super Battle were eligible to compete in a Best in Japan Deciding Match in late August 2000, while overall winners of Tropical Mega Battle regional events represented Japan in the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii; this dossier does not treat Secret Super Battle regional second place as the Hawaii route.

Pokumon describes World Challenge Summer 2000 as a regional tournament circuit across eight Japanese venues, with the juniors championship known as Tropical Mega Battle and the senior-player counterpart as Secret Super Battle Best in Japan.

Pokumon says the card text distinguished Tropical Mega Battle for players aged 14 or under from Secret Super Battle for players 15+, supporting the senior-track boundary for Secret Super Battle cards.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.2 Trainer cards were personalized with the winner's name and regional conference and were Non Holofoil.

Bulbapedia says two base versions of the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.2 Trainer exist, one depicting a male Trainer and the other a female Trainer, with the awarded version depending on the winner's gender.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.2 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori.

Bulbapedia describes Ken Sugimori as a friend of Satoshi Tajiri, illustrator of the original Pokémon game artwork, illustrator of TCG cards and merchandise, and the artist who redrew all 151 Generation I Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use.

Pokumon says Girl SSB No.2 Trainer (World Challenge Summer 2000) was never officially distributed because there were no female winners for 2000 SSB, while one has surfaced for sale without the name and regional text; this dossier records that as collector-source identity context, not official distribution proof.

Pokumon says Secret Super Battle Best in Japan was held at Pokémon Center Tokyo on August 19, 2000 and that winners of that final event received No.1-3 Trainer trophy cards reported to be cosmos holofoil with the winner's photograph printed onto them, but no photos have surfaced to confirm that report.

Pokumon identifies Boy SSB No.2 Trainer and Girl SSB No.2 Trainer as World Challenge Secret Super Battle 2000 regional second-place prize records, Japanese unnumbered non-holo Trainer cards illustrated by Ken Sugimori, and gives estimated copy counts or distribution caveats; this dossier treats those as collector estimates and caveats, not official disclosure.

As judged collector texture, the regional Secret Super Battle No.2 Trainer matters because it preserves senior-track proximity: a high-ranking older-player result close enough to the top to become a personalized trophy, while still distinct from both the champion card and the final-stage photo cards.

narrative.human_title: No.2 Trainer [World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional]: senior-track near-win
narrative.why_it_matters: The Secret Super Battle No.2 Trainer has the ache of a serious near-win. It is not the junior Hawaii story, and it is not the later Best in Japan photo trophy; it is the senior regional circuit recording the player who came just short of first. That makes the card emotionally precise: age lane, rank, region, name, gendered base art, and Sugimori artwork all have to be read together before the card can be understood.
not_claiming: that every No.2 Trainer listing uses this same route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says No.2 Trainer, World Challenge, Secret Super Battle, SSB, regional second place, runner-up, senior division, 15+, personalized name, Best in Japan, photo trophy, female SSB, unused print, or Tropical Mega Battle.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat No.2 Trainer as a reusable trophy-card title. Establish the Secret Super Battle regional runner-up route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is No.2 Trainer / Ｎｏ.２トレーナー and that the claimed promotion is World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional second-place prize, not Tropical Mega Battle, Secret Super Battle Best in Japan, Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, or World Championships.

Check whether the card is the 2000 World Challenge Summer regional Secret Super Battle version: non-holo, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and based on male or female Trainer artwork depending on winner gender.
Keep the age-route split legible: Pokumon describes Tropical Mega Battle as for players aged 14 or under and Secret Super Battle as for players 15+.
Do not treat Secret Super Battle regional second place as the Hawaii representative slot. Bulbapedia assigns the Hawaii / World Exchange Battle path to overall Tropical Mega Battle regional winners.

Separate this regional non-holo card from Secret Super Battle Best in Japan final cards, which Pokumon reports as possible cosmos holofoil photo trophies and explicitly marks as unconfirmed by surfaced photos.

If evaluating a Girl SSB No.2 claim, preserve Pokumon's report that no female winners existed for 2000 SSB and that a surfaced example lacked name and regional text; do not silently promote that into an officially distributed winner card.
Record Pokumon gendered-version copy counts only as collector estimates. Do not convert them into official print-run facts.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including name/conference personalization, front/back, surface, edge, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.

claims.text: The local catalog row identifies source index 178 as No.2 Trainer from the World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional second-place prize slice.
Bulbapedia gives the Japanese name as Ｎｏ.２トレーナー and describes No.2 Trainer as a Japanese tournament Trainer/Item card lineage used for runner-up prizes.

Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.2 Trainer regional cards were personalized with the winner's name and regional conference, non-holo, and split into male and female Trainer base versions.
Bulbapedia identifies Ken Sugimori as the artist for the World Challenge Summer No.2 Trainer major iteration.
As interpretive art context, Sugimori's credit gives the senior-track runner-up card a direct line to Pokémon's original visual standard, while the SSB route gives the object its competitive meaning.

This card must be separated from World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle regional No.2 Trainer, Secret Super Battle Best in Japan No.2 Trainer, Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, World Championships No.2 Trainer, and name-only No.2 Trainer listings.

As judged collector texture, No.2 Trainer [World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional second place] is interesting because it records senior-track proximity to the top: not champion, not junior Hawaii lane, not final photo trophy, but still a personalized regional result.

narrative.human_title: No.2 Trainer: the senior near-win with a caveat
narrative.why_it_matters: This card has a beautiful tension. It is a second-place trophy from the older-player Secret Super Battle route, so it already carries the ache of a serious near-win. Then the source record adds another wrinkle: some gendered versions may be unused or leftover rather than cleanly awarded. That is exactly why the catalog needs special identification instructions. The card is not less interesting because the path is complicated; the complication is the history.
